title: Find Edges in Shortest Paths
summary: Given an undirected weighted graph with n nodes and m edges, determine which edges are part of at least one shortest path from node 0 to node n-1.
statement: Given an undirected weighted graph with n nodes and m edges, determine which edges are part of at least one shortest path from node 0 to node n-1. Return a boolean array indicating true for edges in any shortest path and false otherwise, noting the graph may not be fully connected.
constraints: n≥2 and edges is an undirected positive-weight edge list in input order; the graph may be disconnected or contain parallel edges.
Return one Boolean per edge indicating whether that exact edge belongs to at least one shortest path from node zero to node n-1.
If the destination is unreachable, every result is false.
hints: An undirected edge lies on a shortest route iff one orientation joins a shortest prefix and suffix with exact total distance.
Run Dijkstra from both endpoints, then test each input edge in both orientations.
Any marked equality concatenates into a shortest path, and every edge on a shortest path satisfies one orientation equality.
editorial: Any marked equality concatenates into a shortest path, and every edge on a shortest path satisfies one orientation equality.
